source.text: Ἔλεγεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς πεπιστευκότας αὐτῷ Ἰουδαίους· Ἐὰν ὑμεῖς μείνητε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ ἐμῷ, ἀληθῶς μαθηταί μού ἐστε, καὶ γνώσεσθε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Was saying therefore the Jesus to the [ones] having believed him Jews, "If you remain in the word the my, truly disciples of me you are, \v 32 and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you."

en.L: So Jesus was saying to the Jews who had believed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If you remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, truly you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples, \v 32 and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you."

en.R: Jesus spoke to the Jews in the crowd who had believed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "If you remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word and live by it, you really are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples. \v 32 You will know the truth, and the truth will free you."

decisions.choice: the Jews: Jewish people in the crowd at the temple in Jerusalem who had just come to believe Jesus
decisions.reason: This occurrence does not mean the authorities, and it does not mean the Jewish people as a whole. John has just said that as Jesus spoke in the temple (8:20) many believed in him (8:30); these are the people he now turns to. They are Jews, as Jesus himself, his disciples and his mother are.

decisions.choice: had believed him: the same believers as in 8:30, though the wording changes
alternatives: the change marks a weaker, merely outward belief
decisions.reason: 8:30 says that many "believed in him"; here John writes "having believed him", the perfect participle with the plain dative. In John the two ways of speaking often overlap (compare 5:24 with 6:29), so the change of wording does not by itself show a weaker belief. What follows does show that this new belief is tested at once: Jesus makes remaining in his word the mark of a true disciple, and the talk turns hard (8:33, 37). Whether John means the change of wording to hint at that is uncertain.

decisions.choice: remain in my word: keep holding to Jesus's message and living by it
decisions.reason: Starting to believe is not yet the whole of discipleship; a true disciple stays with what Jesus says. "Remain" is one of John's key verbs (6:56; 15:4-10), and 8:35 picks it up again: the slave does not remain in the house, the son remains. "Word" is Jesus's message as a whole, which he received from the Father (8:26, 28, 38). "Truly" means really, in fact, as opposed to in name only.

decisions.choice: the truth will free you: the truth that Jesus reveals sets people free from slavery to sin
decisions.reason: Knowing the truth is not learning a fact but coming to know God as Jesus makes him known (1:17-18; 17:3); Jesus himself is the truth (14:6). The freedom is explained in 8:34-36: freedom from slavery to sin, given by the Son. The hearers take it as political or social freedom (8:33).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the truth will free you
alternatives: the truth will set you free
the truth will make you free
decisions.reason: The verb is "free", the same word Jesus uses in 8:36 ("if the Son frees you") and the root of "free" in 8:33 and 8:36; the plain verb keeps the three verses visibly linked. "Set you free" or "make you free", the familiar wording, means the same.

decisions.choice: in the crowd; remain in my word and live by it
decisions.reason: Readable says where these Jews were (8:20, 30) and adds "and live by it" to explain what remaining in a word means (meaning decision m3). "Remain" itself is kept, since 8:35 plays on it.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L, B); los judíos de la multitud (R); no "dirigentes"
decisions.reason: Here the word means people in the crowd who had just come to believe (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level speaks of leaders.

decisions.choice: los hará libres
decisions.reason: "Libre" is kept as the root in 8:32, 33 and 36, as the English keeps "free".

decisions.choice: permanecer
decisions.reason: John's weighty "remain", as in 6:56, and echoed in 8:35.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B) and the passé composé (R); Literal keeps John's own tenses (the imperfect "disait" here, the historic present "dit" in 8:39); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for this passage (8:31-47). The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense young readers speak and meet first. Literal keeps the imperfect of "was saying" and, as the English Literal does, the present where John tells a past event in the present. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("j’ai vu", "vous avez entendu").

decisions.choice: la vérité vous libérera; libres (8:33); libère ... libres (8:36)
decisions.reason: As the English "free": one verb, "libérer", of the same family as "libre", so that 8:32, 8:33 and 8:36 stay visibly linked (meaning decision m4). "Affranchir" is the older word for freeing a slave and now sounds literary.

decisions.choice: qui l’avaient cru
decisions.reason: French distinguishes "croire quelqu’un" (take someone at his word) from "croire en quelqu’un", much as the Greek dative here differs from the construction of 8:30. Meaning decision m2 says the change need not mean a weaker belief, but French can keep John's wording visible without deciding it.

decisions.choice: mkikaa katika neno langu
decisions.reason: The verb is "remain", John's word for a lasting union (6:56; 15:4). Swahili "kukaa" has served it since 1:32, so "kukaa katika neno langu" keeps that thread; "kulishika" (keep it) would be the verb of verse 51.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls his hearers "các người" and himself "Ta"; they call him "ông" and themselves "chúng tôi" (8:33-59)
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms for Jesus speaking to crowds and opponents. These hearers had just believed, so a warmer "các anh" is possible here, but the same conversation turns hostile within a few verses and Vietnamese cannot change the relationship mid-scene.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} when he speaks of himself; plain "Ta"/"Ngài" at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: Vietnamese spans of the deity_pronoun setting differ from the English ones: only the capital letter changes. "Ông", the opponents' word for him, is an ordinary title and takes no span.

decisions.choice: "chân lý" for truth
decisions.reason: The book-wide key term. "Lẽ thật" is the familiar 1926 word but sounds dated; "sự thật" means a plain fact, while Jesus speaks of the truth that he reveals.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun alternatives, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and God is carried at every level by the subject honorific -si-, by "께서" and by "그분".

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to his hearers in the plain style (해라체: -다, -느냐) throughout this passage
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide's book-wide speech level for Jesus speaking to crowds and opponents. The narrator uses the honorific for Jesus (말씀하셨다); Jesus does not use it of himself.

decisions.choice: "내 말 안에 머물다" for "remain in my word"
decisions.reason: "머물다" is the book-wide word for menō. Jesus speaks of his own word as "내 말": a speaker does not use the honorific "말씀" of his own words; the narrator and others say "말씀".

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ ἐσμεν καὶ οὐδενὶ δεδουλεύκαμεν πώποτε· πῶς σὺ λέγεις ὅτι Ἐλεύθεροι γενήσεσθε;

records.literal_gloss: They answered to him, "Seed of Abraham we are, and to no one have we been slaves ever; how do you say that, 'Free you will become'?"

en.L: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We are Abraham's seed, and we have never at any time been slaves to anyone. How [is it that] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, 'You will become free'?"
en.B: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We are descended from Abraham, and we have never been slaves to anybody. What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean, 'You will become free'?"
en.R: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We come from Abraham's family, and we have never been anyone's slaves. What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say that we will become free?"

es.L: Le respondieron: «Descendencia de Abraham somos, y jamás hemos sido esclavos de nadie. ¿Cómo dices {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}: “{{plural_you:Llegarán|Llegaréis}} a ser libres”?».
es.B: Le respondieron: «Somos descendientes de Abraham, y nunca hemos sido esclavos de nadie. ¿Qué quieres decir con eso de: “{{plural_you:Llegarán|Llegaréis}} a ser libres”?».
es.R: Le respondieron: «Somos de la familia de Abraham, y nunca hemos sido esclavos de nadie. ¿Qué quieres decir cuando dices que llegaremos a ser libres?».

vi.B: Họ đáp: "Chúng tôi là con cháu Áp-ra-ham, và chưa hề làm nô lệ cho ai cả. Sao ông lại nói: 'Các người sẽ được tự do'?"

ko.L: 그들이 그분께 대답했다. "우리는 아브라함의 씨이고, 지금까지 아무에게도 종이 된 적이 없습니다. 어떻게 '너희가 자유롭게 될 것이다' 하고 말씀하십니까?"
ko.B: 그들이 그분께 대답했다. "우리는 아브라함의 자손이고, 지금까지 누구의 종이 된 적도 없습니다. 그런데 '너희가 자유롭게 될 것이다'라니, 무슨 말씀입니까?"
ko.R: 그들이 그분께 대답했다. "우리는 아브라함 집안의 자손입니다. 우리는 한 번도 누구의 종이었던 적이 없습니다. 그런데 우리가 자유롭게 될 것이라니, 그게 무슨 말씀입니까?"

decisions.choice: they answered: the hearers of 8:31, with the crowd around them
alternatives: the crowd as a whole, no longer the new believers
decisions.reason: John does not change the subject, so the reply comes from those Jesus has just spoken to, the people who had believed him (8:31). As the talk goes on, Jesus says "you are seeking to kill me" (8:37, 40), which fits those in the temple crowd and among the authorities who were already seeking his death (7:1, 19-20, 25, 30). The text does not say exactly where the line runs between the new believers and the others listening; it is plain only that the replies come from people in that crowd.

decisions.choice: seed of Abraham: Abraham's descendants, heirs of God's promise to him
decisions.reason: "Seed" is the Bible's word for descendants (Genesis 12:7; 15:5; 22:17-18). To be Abraham's seed was to belong to the people God had chosen and promised to bless. Jesus grants that they are (8:37); the question he raises is what kind of children they are (8:39).

decisions.choice: never slaves to anyone: a claim to free standing that their own history did not bear out
decisions.reason: Israel had been slaves in Egypt (Exodus 20:2, "out of the house of slavery"), had been taken into exile in Babylon, and in Jesus's day lived under Roman rule. The hearers most likely mean that as Abraham's descendants they had never been anyone's property, whatever foreign power ruled them. Jesus answers on another level: the slavery he means is slavery to sin (8:34).

decisions.choice: descended from Abraham (B); come from Abraham's family (R)
decisions.reason: "Seed" (Literal) is the Bible's own picture, but in everyday speech it does not mean descendants; Balanced and Readable say it plainly (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: What do you mean ...?
decisions.reason: The question "how do you say" is a protest, not a request for information; Balanced and Readable put it the way English protests. Literal keeps "How [is it that] you say".

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: the hearers deny ever being slaves in answer to "you will become free" (m3; 8:32-36).

decisions.choice: descendencia (L); descendientes (B); de la familia de Abraham (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "seed" means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: [la] descendance d’Abraham
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "seed", the Bible's picture for descendants (meaning decision m2). French "semence" is now an agricultural word and would read oddly, and "postérité" is old-fashioned; "descendance" says the same thing in the singular, as the Greek does. Balanced and Readable follow the English.

decisions.choice: Abrahamu (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Ibrahimu" is the older Swahili Bible spelling and the usual Muslim form; "Abrahamu" is the form in newer Swahili Bibles and is closer to the Greek and Hebrew. Already used at 7:22.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Áp-ra-ham" (B); "thuộc dòng dõi Áp-ra-ham" (R); "dòng dõi" (L)
decisions.reason: "Hạt giống" (seed) is not used of descendants in modern Vietnamese; "dòng dõi" keeps the collective sense of the Greek.

decisions.choice: These hearers still address Jesus in the formal style (합쇼체: -습니다, -십니까) in 8:33-41
alternatives: the plain style (해라체) from here on
decisions.reason: They had just come to believe him (8:30-31), so their first replies stay formal even as they bristle. When the exchange turns to open insult in 8:48, they drop the honorifics.

decisions.choice: everyone who does sin: a person whose life is given over to sin
alternatives: anyone who commits a single sin
decisions.reason: The present participle with "the sin" describes someone who goes on doing sin, a settled way of living, not a single wrong act. 1 John uses the same phrase (1 John 3:4, 8-9). Jesus is not singling out his hearers here: the saying is about everyone.

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master, with no rights of his own
decisions.reason: δοῦλός is the word for a slave, someone who was another's property and could be bought, sold or sent away (8:35). Here the master is sin itself. Jesus answers their claim never to have been slaves (8:33): the slavery that matters is not to a foreign power but to sin.

decisions.choice: a slave of sin (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Nearly all manuscripts have "of sin". A few witnesses leave it out, among them Codex Bezae and some early versions, which gives "everyone who does sin is a slave" and leads straight into the household picture of 8:35. The sense is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery to sin is set against freedom (8:32, 36): Jesus says that such a person is owned. Meaning decision m2 says what a slave's position was.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering, recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: esclavo
decisions.reason: As in English: "esclavo" at every level, since slavery to sin is set against freedom here (8:32, 36; meaning decision m2).

alternatives: Amen, amen, je vous le dis
Oui, vraiment, je vous le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John, recorded once in this passage. Readable puts the pledge in plain words.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R)

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level in 8:33-35

decisions.reason: Here the word is set against "free" and "son": the point is slavery, and "đầy tớ" (servant) would lose it. The English keeps "slave" at every level here too.

decisions.reason: The book-wide Korean choice for amen amen: modern plain-style ending instead of the archaic "이르노니"; Readable says the same solemn assurance in everyday words.

decisions.choice: a household picture: a slave has no lasting place in the house; a son belongs to it
decisions.reason: In a household of the time a slave belonged to the family as property and could be sold or sent away at the master's will; a son was the heir and belonged there for good. Jesus moves from "slave of sin" (8:34) to this everyday picture: a slave's place is never secure.

decisions.choice: possibly Abraham's own household: Ishmael sent away, Isaac the heir (Genesis 21:10)
decisions.reason: The hearers have just claimed to be Abraham's seed (8:33). In Abraham's house the son of the slave woman was sent away while Isaac remained as heir (Genesis 21:10-12), and Paul draws on the same story (Galatians 4:21-31). John does not name it, so the echo is possible but not certain; the picture makes sense as ordinary household life.

decisions.choice: the son: a general picture that points to Jesus, the Son
alternatives: the Son: Jesus only, not a general picture
decisions.reason: Like "the slave", "the son" is any son of a household. But 8:36 applies it at once to Jesus, the Son who can free slaves; the picture is told with him in view. "Remains" picks up 8:31: the disciple who remains in Jesus's word shares the place of the son.

decisions.choice: son (lowercase)
decisions.reason: In 8:35 "son" is part of the picture of any household, so it is not capitalised; in 8:36 it refers to Jesus and is written "Son" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: for good (B); forever (L, R)
decisions.reason: "For good" says that the slave's stay is never permanent, which is the point of "into the age" here; Literal and Readable keep "forever". Readable adds "A slave can be sent away", the reason a slave does not remain (meaning decision m1), and "the family's house" for the household.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: the slave who can be sent away is set against the son who belongs, and against the Son who sets people free (8:34, 36; m1).

decisions.choice: hijo, lower case; permanecer
decisions.reason: As in English: here "hijo" is part of the household picture, so it is not capitalized; in 8:36 it is Jesus. "Permanecer" keeps the echo of 8:31.

decisions.choice: demeure (R, as L and B)
decisions.reason: "Demeurer" is more literary than "rester", but Jesus picks up the verb of 8:31 ("si vous demeurez dans ma parole"; meaning decision m3), so Readable keeps it in both verses, as the English Readable keeps "remain".

decisions.choice: "người con" (a son, lowercase)
decisions.reason: The picture is a general one about a household; the capital comes in 8:36 when Jesus applies it to himself.

decisions.choice: the Son: Jesus, the Son of the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus now applies the picture of 8:35 to himself. Only one who belongs to the house for good can set its slaves free; the Son has that place with the Father (3:35; 5:19-23). In 8:32 the truth frees; here the Son does: Jesus is himself the truth (14:6).

decisions.choice: really free: free in fact, not only in name
decisions.reason: The adverb means "in reality". It answers the hearers' claim that they had never been slaves (8:33): the freedom they claim is outward, while the freedom the Son gives is freedom from slavery to sin (8:34).

decisions.choice: Son (capitalised)
decisions.reason: Here "the son" of 8:35 is Jesus himself, so every level writes "Son". "Frees" is the same verb as in 8:32.

decisions.choice: el Hijo, capitalized; hace libres
decisions.reason: The son of 8:35 is now Jesus himself. "Hacer libres" is the same verb as in 8:32.

decisions.choice: "아들" in 8:35 and 8:36 alike
decisions.reason: English marks the move from the household picture to Jesus with a capital "Son"; Korean has no capitals. The same word is kept and, as in the Greek, the context shows that the Son who frees is Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus grants that they are Abraham's descendants
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny their descent from Abraham. The question he raises in what follows (8:39-44) is not who their ancestors are but whose works they are doing.

decisions.choice: you seek to kill me: said to those in the crowd who were seeking his death
alternatives: every one of the new believers of 8:31 sought his death
decisions.reason: The plural "you" is the people Jesus is speaking with in the temple. The attempt on his life was already under way: the authorities wanted to kill him (5:18; 7:1) and had sent officers to arrest him (7:32), and some of the people of Jerusalem knew it (7:25). The text does not say that every listener, or the new believers of 8:31, shared that aim; it holds that this crowd as a whole was not receiving his word. At the end of the chapter some of them pick up stones (8:59).

decisions.choice: my word has no room in you: you do not make room for my word, so it cannot take hold
alternatives: my word makes no progress among you
decisions.reason: The verb χωρεῖ means to have room, to find a place, or to make headway. Either way the sense is that Jesus's word is not received; that is why they want to be rid of him.

decisions.choice: is making no headway in you (B); you have no room in you for my word (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the picture of progress, Readable that of room; both are senses of the verb (meaning decision m3), and both say the word is not received.

decisions.choice: no logra abrirse paso (B); no tienen lugar (R); no tiene cabida (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: two senses of the verb, making headway and having room (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: ne fait pas son chemin en vous
decisions.reason: The French idiom "faire son chemin" (to make headway, to take hold in someone's mind) gives the English Balanced's picture of progress in everyday words (meaning decision m3). Literal and Readable keep the picture of room, "place".

decisions.choice: "không thấm vào lòng các người" (does not soak into your hearts)
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese image for a word that makes no headway in a person.

decisions.choice: the Father ... the father, without possessives (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have no possessives. Many later manuscripts read "my Father" in the first half and "your father" in the second, which makes plain that two different fathers are meant. Some also read "what you have seen" for "what you heard". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you do: a statement contrasting two fathers, the father named in 8:44
alternatives: a command: so you too must do what you heard from the Father
decisions.reason: The verb can be a statement ("you do") or a command ("so you too must do"). Read as a command, both fathers are God, and Jesus urges them to do what they have heard from the Father. Read as a statement, as here, Jesus contrasts his Father with theirs, whom he names in 8:44; the next verses support this, since they protest that their father is Abraham (8:39) and Jesus answers that they do the works of their father (8:41). The difference matters, and the evidence is not decisive.

decisions.choice: what I have seen with the Father: Jesus speaks from his own presence with God
decisions.reason: Jesus has been with the Father and speaks what he has seen and heard there (1:18; 3:11, 32; 8:26, 28). The hearers, by contrast, act on what they "heard" from another source.

decisions.choice: the Father (capitalised) ... the father (lowercase)
alternatives: the Father in both places (if the verb is a command)
decisions.reason: Capital letters are a choice the Greek does not make. Following meaning decision m2, the first father is God and is capitalised; the second is the other father of 8:44 and is not. Readable supplies "my" and "your", as many manuscripts have them (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el Padre ... el padre

decisions.choice: if you are ... you would be doing (SBLGNT)
alternatives: if you were Abraham's children, you would be doing
if you are Abraham's children, do the works of Abraham
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ in both verbs. The SBLGNT reads "if you are ... you would be doing", a mixed form that implies they are not doing Abraham's works. Some manuscripts read "if you were ... you would be doing", a plain condition contrary to fact; others read "if you are ... do the works of Abraham", a command. All three say that Abraham's true children act like him. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: children of Abraham: those who share Abraham's character, not only his descent
decisions.reason: Jesus has granted that they are Abraham's seed (8:37); now he speaks of being his children, which in the Bible's way of speaking means resembling a father in what one does. The same thought is in 8:41 and 8:44, and Paul speaks of Abraham's children in a similar way (Romans 4:11-12; Galatians 3:7).

decisions.choice: the works of Abraham: Abraham believed God and welcomed those God sent
decisions.reason: Abraham trusted and obeyed God's word (Genesis 12:1-4; 15:6; 22:1-18) and received God's messengers with hospitality (Genesis 18:1-8). 8:40 makes the contrast: they seek to kill one who brings them the truth from God.

decisions.choice: said (B, R); says (Literal)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("says"). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English narrative does. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: If you really are
decisions.reason: Readable adds "really" to bring out the challenge in the mixed condition (meaning decision m1): Jesus doubts that they are Abraham's children in the full sense.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Si son ... harían
decisions.reason: Spanish can keep the Greek mixed condition ("if you are ... you would be doing"), so every level does (meaning decision m1). "Hijos" already includes daughters, as at 1:12.

decisions.choice: Si vous êtes ... vous feriez (L); Si vous êtes ... vous devriez faire (B, R)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT mixes a real condition with an unreal result (meaning decision m1). French grammar does not allow "si" with the present followed by the conditional, but Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does, so that readers see the mixed form. Balanced and Readable use "vous devriez faire", which is correct French and keeps the same implication: they are not doing Abraham's works.

decisions.choice: historic present: Literal "nói" without "đã"; Balanced and Readable "bảo", read as past from the story
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs carry no tense, so the historic present shows only in the absence of a past marker; one decision for this passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal ("말씀하신다"); past tense at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean narrative can use the present for vividness, so Literal keeps John's tense; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary past. One decision per passage.

decisions.choice: this Abraham did not do: Abraham did not reject God's messenger

decisions.choice: not born of sexual immorality: they deny being unfaithful to God, perhaps with a jab at Jesus's birth
alternatives: a plain claim about their own birth and descent
chiefly an insult about Jesus's birth
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel's turning to other gods sexual unfaithfulness, and its people "children of whoredom" (Hosea 1:2; 2:4). The hearers answer that they are no such children: they worship the one God and he alone is their Father (Malachi 2:10). The emphatic "we" may also hint "unlike you": Jesus's mother was found to be with child before her marriage (Matthew 1:18-19), and the hearers will go on to insult him (8:48). The text does not make that hint explicit, so it remains a possibility.

decisions.choice: one Father, God: they claim God himself as their Father
decisions.reason: God is called Israel's Father in Scripture (Deuteronomy 32:6; Isaiah 63:16; 64:8). Having been told that their deeds do not match Abraham, they reach past him to God. Jesus answers that claim in 8:42.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality (L); sexual sin (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word covers every kind of sexual sin, including prostitution, and the prophets use it for idolatry (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable use the plainer phrase; "illegitimate" would decide for one reading of the sentence.

decisions.choice: fornicación (L); inmoralidad sexual (B); pecado sexual (R)

decisions.choice: l’immoralité sexuelle (L); l’inconduite sexuelle (B); un péché sexuel (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers every kind of sexual sin, and the prophets use it for Israel's unfaithfulness to God (meaning decision m1). "Prostitution" narrows it to one sin, and "enfants illégitimes" would decide that they are only taunting Jesus about his birth, which m1 leaves as a possible undertone.

decisions.choice: "음행" (L); "음란한 관계" (B); "부정한 관계" (R)
decisions.reason: The words keep the open phrase "born of sexual immorality" without spelling out the possible jab at Jesus's birth, which the meaning decision and its footnote explain.

en.B: Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I came out from God and have arrived here. I have not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own authority; it was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "If God really were your Father, you would love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I came from God, and now I am here. I did not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. God sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Jesús les dijo: «Si Dios fuera {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}, me {{plural_you:amarían|amaríais}}, porque yo salí de Dios y he venido; pues no he venido por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, sino que aquel me envió.
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Si Dios fuera {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}, me {{plural_you:amarían|amaríais}}, porque yo salí de Dios y aquí estoy. No he venido por mi propia cuenta; fue {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quien me envió.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Si de verdad Dios fuera {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}, me {{plural_you:amarían|amaríais}}. Yo vine de Dios, y ahora estoy aquí. No vine por mi propia cuenta. Dios me envió.

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « Si Dieu était votre Père, vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimeriez, car {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis sorti de Dieu et je suis là ; car je ne suis pas venu de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, mais c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Si Dieu était votre Père, vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimeriez, car je suis sorti de Dieu et {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} voici. Je ne suis pas venu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre autorité ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Si Dieu était vraiment votre Père, vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimeriez. Je suis venu de Dieu, et maintenant je suis ici. Je ne suis pas venu de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}. C’est Dieu qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.

decisions.choice: if God were your Father, you would love me: implying that, in this sense, he is not
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence is contrary to fact. A true child of God would recognise and love the one who comes from God (compare 5:42-43; 1 John 5:1). Jesus judges the claim of 8:41 by the same test of family likeness as in 8:39.

decisions.choice: I came out from God and am here: Jesus's origin with God and his coming into the world
decisions.reason: "Came out from God" speaks of where he comes from (13:3; 16:27-28); "am here" says that he has arrived and is present among them.

decisions.choice: not of myself, but he sent me: Jesus comes as the Father's envoy
decisions.reason: Jesus did not come on his own initiative or authority (5:30; 7:28-29). The one who sent him is God, the Father he has just spoken of; "that one" is how John often refers to God or to Jesus.

decisions.choice: God sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names God where the Greek says "that one", and adds "really" in the first line to bring out the contrary-to-fact form (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el Padre de ustedes / vuestro Padre
decisions.reason: "Su Padre" could be read as "his Father"; the span keeps the owner plain.

decisions.choice: Dios me envió; de verdad
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names God for "aquel" and brings out the contrary-to-fact condition.

decisions.choice: c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui m’a envoyé
decisions.reason: The Greek "that one" refers to God. French "celui-là" would sound dismissive, so Literal and Balanced say "c’est lui qui", a pronoun for God that takes the setting, as the English "he" does. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} when Jesus speaks of the Father
decisions.reason: The narrator's pronoun for God serves in Jesus's mouth too; it keeps the Father distinct from "Ta".

decisions.reason: "Hear" in Scripture often means to listen and obey (Deuteronomy 6:4). They hear the sounds, but they cannot accept the message. In John, such inability goes with an unwillingness of the heart (5:40, 44; 12:39-40), as 8:44 says: they want to do another's desires.

decisions.choice: entendre (L, R); écouter (B), with "ne supportez pas" (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "entendre" is to hear sounds, "écouter" to listen. Literal keeps the plain "entendre"; Balanced says "écouter" because the point is listening and accepting (meaning decision m1), and both Balanced and Readable add "supporter", as the English adds "bear" and "stand", so that it is not read as a matter of the ears. The same pairing holds in 8:47.

decisions.choice: said to these hearers who are seeking to kill him: it names whose works they are doing, not their descent or their people
alternatives: a statement about the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Jesus has granted that they are Abraham's descendants (8:37), and he has been judging fatherhood by works throughout (8:39, 41). The works in question are seeking to kill a man who speaks the truth (8:37, 40), and murder and lying are what this verse goes on to say are the devil's own works. So the charge is about what these particular hearers are doing to Jesus, not about who their ancestors are and not about a people. The same language is used of anyone who does such deeds: 1 John 3:8-12 says that whoever does sin is "of the devil" and gives Cain as the example; Jesus calls Peter "Satan" (Matthew 16:23) and says that one of the Twelve is a devil (6:70). The text does not say that the Jewish people are children of the devil: Jesus, his disciples and his mother are Jews, and many in this same crowd had just believed him (8:30).

decisions.choice: of the father, the devil: the devil is the father, not the father of the devil
alternatives: of the father of the devil
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand side by side, "the father, the devil", and the second names the first. The words could be read as "of the father of the devil", but nothing in John speaks of such a figure, and the rest of the verse describes the devil himself as the father.

decisions.choice: you want to do his desires: they choose what he wants
decisions.reason: "Want" is the verb of will and choice. They are not helpless; they are willing to carry out what the devil desires, and the next sentence says what that is: killing and lying.

decisions.choice: Your father is the devil

You are of your father the devil (Literal)

decisions.choice: del padre, el diablo (L)

decisions.choice: El padre de ustedes es el diablo

decisions.choice: "ma quỷ" for the devil

decisions.choice: a murderer from the beginning: the devil brought death into the world (Genesis 3), and his work showed in Cain (Genesis 4:8)
decisions.reason: In Genesis 3 the serpent's lie led to human death (Genesis 2:17; 3:4, 19); in Genesis 4:8 Cain killed his brother, and 1 John 3:12 says Cain "was of the evil one". Either or both may be in view. The word means a killer of human beings, and it ties back to 8:37 and 8:40: those who seek to kill Jesus are doing the devil's work.

decisions.choice: did not stand in the truth: he never held his ground in it
alternatives: he does not stand in the truth
decisions.reason: The source data parses ἔστηκεν as an imperfect: he did not stand, or was not standing, in the truth. Early manuscripts have no accents or breathings, and with a different breathing the same letters are a perfect, "he does not stand". Either way the devil has no footing in the truth, and the reason follows: there is no truth in him.

decisions.choice: has never kept to the truth
decisions.reason: Readable puts "not stand in the truth" in plain words.

decisions.choice: nunca se ha mantenido en la verdad
decisions.reason: As in English: puts "not stand in the truth" in plain words (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: il ne se tenait pas
decisions.reason: Literal follows the source data, which parses the verb as an imperfect (meaning decision m2); the French imperfect says he was not standing in the truth. Balanced and Readable say "never", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nó" and "kẻ" for the devil
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks contempt in the pronoun; "nó" is the ordinary pronoun for an evil being, and the Greek ekeinos is "kẻ ấy" at Literal.

source.text: ὅταν λαλῇ τὸ ψεῦδος, ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων λαλεῖ, ὅτι ψεύστης ἐστὶν καὶ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: When he speaks the lie, from the own [things] he speaks, because a liar he is and the father of it.

en.L: Whenever he speaks the lie, he speaks from his own, because he is a liar and the father of it.
en.B: Whenever he tells a lie, he is speaking from what is his own, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
en.R: When he lies, he is speaking from what he really is. He is a liar, and the father of lies.

es.L: Cuando dice la mentira, habla de lo suyo, porque es mentiroso y padre de ella.
es.B: Cuando dice una mentira, habla de lo que le es propio, porque es mentiroso y padre de la mentira.
es.R: Cuando miente, habla de lo que él realmente es. Es mentiroso, y el padre de la mentira.

fr.L: Quand il dit le mensonge, il parle de ce qui lui est propre, parce qu’il est menteur et qu’il en est le père.
fr.B: Quand il dit un mensonge, il tire ses paroles de ce qui est à lui, car il est menteur et le père du mensonge.
fr.R: Quand il ment, il parle selon ce qu’il est vraiment. C’est un menteur, et le père du mensonge.

sw.L: Kila asemapo uongo, husema kutoka kwa vilivyo vyake, kwa sababu yeye ni mwongo na baba wa huo.
sw.B: Kila anaposema uongo, anasema kutokana na kile alicho, kwa sababu yeye ni mwongo na baba wa uongo.
sw.R: Anaposema uongo, anasema kutokana na jinsi alivyo hasa. Yeye ni mwongo, na baba wa uongo.

vi.L: Khi nó nói điều dối trá, nó nói từ những gì của riêng nó, vì nó là kẻ nói dối và là cha của điều ấy.
vi.B: Mỗi khi nói dối, nó nói theo bản chất của nó, vì nó là kẻ nói dối và là cha của sự dối trá.
vi.R: Khi nói dối, nó nói đúng như bản chất của nó. Nó là kẻ nói dối, và là cha của mọi sự dối trá.

ko.L: 그가 거짓을 말할 때에는 자기 것에서 말한다. 그는 거짓말쟁이요 그것의 아버지이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그가 거짓말을 할 때는 자기 본래의 것에서 말하는 것이다. 그는 거짓말쟁이이고 거짓의 아버지이기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그가 거짓말을 하는 것은 그의 본모습이 그렇기 때문이다. 그는 거짓말쟁이이고, 모든 거짓의 아버지이다.

decisions.choice: the father of it: the father of lying, the one from whom falsehood comes
alternatives: he is a liar, and so is his father
decisions.reason: "Of it" (αὐτοῦ) may point back to "the lie" (falsehood itself) or to "liar" (the father of every liar). Both say that lying starts with him. The words can also be read "he is a liar, and so is his father", but that would give the devil a father, which nothing in Scripture suggests.

decisions.choice: he speaks from his own: lying is his own nature
decisions.reason: Jesus says that he does not speak from himself but what the Father gives him (7:16-18; 8:28; 12:49). The devil is the opposite: when he lies, he is speaking out of what belongs to him.

decisions.choice: the lie: possibly the serpent's first lie (Genesis 3:4)
decisions.reason: The article may simply mark lying in general, or it may recall the lie of Genesis 3:4, "You will not surely die", which goes with "murderer from the beginning".

decisions.choice: the father of lies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "of it" refers to (meaning decision m1). Readable says "from what he really is" for "from his own".

decisions.choice: padre de la mentira (B, R); padre de ella (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what "of it" refers to (meaning decision m1, whose footnote gives the other reading).

decisions.choice: qu’il en est le père
decisions.reason: French "en" can point back to "le mensonge" or to "menteur", as the Greek pronoun can (meaning decision m1), so Literal keeps the open reference. Balanced and Readable say "le père du mensonge", as the English does.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ὅτι τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω, οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι.

records.literal_gloss: I but because the truth I speak, not you believe me.

en.L: But I, because I speak the truth, you do not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But as for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, it is because I tell the truth that you do not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: But I tell you the truth, and that is why you do not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque digo la verdad, no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}.
es.B: Pero en cuanto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, precisamente porque digo la verdad, no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}.
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad, y por eso no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, parce que je dis la vérité, vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez pas.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, c’est justement parce que je dis la vérité que vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez pas.
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous dis la vérité, et c’est pour cela que vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez pas.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa sababu nasema kweli, hamniamini.
sw.B: Lakini kwa upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ni kwa sababu nasema kweli ndiyo maana hamniamini.
sw.R: Lakini mimi nawaambia kweli, na ndiyo sababu hamniamini.

vi.L: Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói chân lý, các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói chân lý mà các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói chân lý cho các người, và vì thế các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러나 나는, 진리를 말하기 때문에, 너희가 나를 믿지 않는다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희가 나를 믿지 않는 것은 바로 내가 진리를 말하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 너희에게 진리를 말한다. 그래서 너희는 나를 믿지 않는다.

decisions.choice: but I ... because: Jesus sets himself against the liar, and the truth is the reason they do not believe
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" contrasts Jesus with the devil of 8:44. One would expect "although I speak the truth"; Jesus says "because": since they belong to the father of lies, the truth itself is what they reject.

decisions.choice: But as for me, it is because ... (B); and that is why (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with "I" and then changes course. Balanced keeps the stress on "me" with "as for me"; Readable makes two clauses. Literal keeps the broken sentence.

decisions.choice: en cuanto a mí, precisamente porque
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps the stress on "mí" and the surprising "because" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐλέγχει με περὶ ἁμαρτίας;

records.literal_gloss: Who of you convicts me concerning sin?

en.L: Who of you convicts {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} of sin?
en.B: Which of you can prove that I have sinned?
en.R: Can any one of you show that I have ever sinned?

es.L: ¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me declara culpable de pecado?
es.B: ¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} puede probar que he pecado?
es.R: ¿Puede alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} demostrar que alguna vez he pecado?

fr.L: Qui d’entre vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} convainc de péché ?
fr.B: Lequel d’entre vous peut prouver que j’ai péché ?
fr.R: Est-ce que l’un de vous peut montrer que j’ai commis un seul péché ?

sw.L: Ni nani kati yenu anayenithibitishia dhambi?
sw.B: Ni nani kati yenu anayeweza kuthibitisha kwamba nimetenda dhambi?
sw.R: Je, yupo hata mmoja wenu anayeweza kuonyesha kwamba nimewahi kutenda dhambi?

vi.L: Ai trong các người bắt lỗi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} về tội lỗi?
vi.B: Ai trong các người có thể chứng minh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có tội?
vi.R: Có ai trong các người chỉ ra được {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã từng phạm tội không?

ko.L: 너희 가운데 누가 죄에 대하여 나를 유죄로 밝히느냐?
ko.B: 너희 가운데 누가 내가 죄를 지었다고 증명할 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 내가 죄를 지은 적이 있다고 보여 줄 수 있는 사람이 너희 가운데 하나라도 있느냐?

decisions.choice: convicts: proves someone guilty
decisions.reason: The verb means to expose or prove guilty, as in a court (16:8). Jesus invites them to bring any charge of wrongdoing against him; under the Law a charge had to be proved (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: sin: wrongdoing of any kind, including speaking falsely
decisions.reason: In this context of truth and lies the word may point especially to falsehood, but it keeps its full sense. It ties back to 8:34: everyone who does sin is its slave, and they cannot show that he is.

decisions.choice: Which of you can prove that I have sinned? (B); Can any one of you show ... (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the challenge as English asks it, with "can"; it is a challenge, not a request for a name.

decisions.choice: me declara culpable
decisions.reason: The verb means to prove guilty, as in a court (meaning decision m1); "redargüir" is now rare.

source.text: εἰ ἀλήθειαν λέγω, διὰ τί ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι;

records.literal_gloss: If truth I speak, why you not believe me?

en.L: If I speak truth, why do you not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: If it is the truth I speak, why do you not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: If I am telling you the truth, then why do you not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Si digo verdad, ¿por qué no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}?
es.B: Si lo que digo es la verdad, ¿por qué no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad, entonces ¿por qué no me {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}?

fr.L: Si je dis vrai, pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez-vous pas ?
fr.B: Si c’est la vérité que je dis, pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez-vous pas ?
fr.R: Si je vous dis la vérité, alors pourquoi est-ce que vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croyez pas ?

sw.L: Ikiwa nasema kweli, mbona hamniamini?
sw.B: Ikiwa ni kweli ninayoisema, kwa nini hamniamini?
sw.R: Kama ninawaambia kweli, basi kwa nini hamniamini?

vi.L: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói chân lý, sao các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.B: Nếu điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói là chân lý, tại sao các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.R: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang nói chân lý với các người, thì tại sao các người không tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?

ko.L: 내가 진리를 말한다면, 어찌하여 너희는 나를 믿지 않느냐?
ko.B: 내가 말하는 것이 진리라면, 어찌하여 너희는 나를 믿지 않느냐?
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 진리를 말하고 있다면, 그런데도 왜 너희는 나를 믿지 않느냐?

decisions.choice: if I speak truth: a real condition; since no fault can be shown, the question is why they do not believe
decisions.reason: The question has no answer they can give; Jesus himself answers it in 8:47.

decisions.choice: speak truth (no article)
decisions.reason: Here the Greek has "truth" without the article, unlike 8:45; Literal shows it. Balanced and Readable say "the truth", as English does.

decisions.choice: digo verdad, no article (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal shows that "truth" has no article here.

decisions.choice: Si je dis vrai
decisions.reason: The Greek has "truth" without the article here, unlike 8:45. French "dire vrai" (to speak truly) has no article either, so Literal can show the difference in natural French.

source.text: ὁ ὢν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούει· διὰ τοῦτο ὑμεῖς οὐκ ἀκούετε ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἐστέ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] being of the God the words of the God hears; for this you not hear, because of the God not you are."

en.L: The one who is of God hears the words of God; for this reason you do not hear, because you are not of God."
en.B: Anyone who comes from God listens to God's words. You do not listen, and this is why: you are not from God."
en.R: People who belong to God listen to God's words. But you do not listen to them, because you do not belong to God."

es.L: El que es de Dios oye las palabras de Dios; por esto {{plural_you:ustedes no oyen|vosotros no oís}}, porque no {{plural_you:son|sois}} de Dios».
es.B: El que viene de Dios escucha las palabras de Dios. {{plural_you:Ustedes no escuchan|Vosotros no escucháis}}, y la razón es esta: no {{plural_you:son|sois}} de Dios».
es.R: Los que pertenecen a Dios escuchan las palabras de Dios. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no las escuchan|vosotros no las escucháis}}, porque no {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} a Dios».

fr.L: Celui qui est de Dieu entend les paroles de Dieu ; c’est pour cela que vous, vous n’entendez pas : parce que vous n’êtes pas de Dieu. »
fr.B: Celui qui vient de Dieu écoute les paroles de Dieu. Vous, vous n’écoutez pas, et voici pourquoi : vous ne venez pas de Dieu. »
fr.R: Ceux qui appartiennent à Dieu écoutent les paroles de Dieu. Mais vous, vous ne les écoutez pas, parce que vous n’appartenez pas à Dieu. »

sw.L: Aliye wa Mungu huyasikia maneno ya Mungu; kwa sababu hii ninyi hamyasikii, kwa kuwa ninyi si wa Mungu."
sw.B: Yeyote anayetoka kwa Mungu husikiliza maneno ya Mungu. Ninyi hamsikilizi, na sababu ni hii: ninyi si wa Mungu."
sw.R: Watu walio wa Mungu husikiliza maneno ya Mungu. Lakini ninyi hamyasikilizi, kwa sababu ninyi si wa Mungu."

vi.L: Ai thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời thì nghe những lời của Đức Chúa Trời; vì lý do này các người không nghe, vì các người không thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Ai đến từ Đức Chúa Trời thì lắng nghe lời Đức Chúa Trời. Các người không lắng nghe, và lý do là: các người không đến từ Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Ai thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời thì lắng nghe lời Đức Chúa Trời. Nhưng các người không lắng nghe, vì các người không thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 하나님께 속한 사람은 하나님의 말씀들을 듣는다. 너희가 듣지 않는 이유는 이것이다. 너희가 하나님께 속하지 않았기 때문이다."
ko.B: 하나님께로부터 온 사람은 하나님의 말씀을 귀담아듣는다. 너희가 듣지 않는 것은 이 때문이다. 너희가 하나님께로부터 오지 않았기 때문이다."
ko.R: 하나님께 속한 사람들은 하나님의 말씀을 듣는다. 그러나 너희는 듣지 않는다. 너희가 하나님께 속하지 않았기 때문이다."

decisions.choice: of God: belonging to God, born of him
decisions.reason: To be "of God" is to have one's life from God (1:12-13; 3:3-8) and so to share his character; the same language is in 1 John 3:10 and 4:6. A person's response to God's words shows where he comes from.

decisions.choice: hear: listen and accept
decisions.reason: As in 8:43, hearing means taking the words to heart. They hear Jesus speak but do not receive what he says.

decisions.choice: you are not of God: said to these hearers, who reject the words of the one God sent
alternatives: a statement about the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The "you" is the same group as in 8:37-44: those in the crowd who are seeking to kill him and will not hear him. It is a judgment on their present response, not on a people: in John, Jews in Jerusalem keep coming to believe (8:30; 11:45; 12:11, 42).

decisions.choice: comes from God (B); belong to God (R)
decisions.reason: "Is of God" (Literal) is not everyday English. Balanced says where such a person comes from, Readable whom they belong to; both are part of the sense (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: viene de Dios (B); pertenecen a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "ser de Dios" is plain in Spanish, but Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m1).
